overview: Understanding the evolution from basic generative models to sophisticated autonomous agent systems.
summary: Understanding the evolution from basic generative models to sophisticated autonomous agent systems.

slides.title: Explaining Key AI Concepts
slides.content:
Goal is to simplify three important AI terms.
Differentiate between Generative AI, AI Agent, and Agentic AI.
Understand the capabilities and complexities of each system.
Explore practical examples for better comprehension.

slides.title: What is Generative AI?
slides.content:
Creates new content based on learned data patterns.
Generates text, images, videos, and more.
Powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4.
Trained on vast volumes of internet data.
Produces answers based on its training knowledge.

slides.title: LLM Limitations
slides.content:
Generative AI with only LLM has knowledge cut-off dates.
Cannot provide real-time information or current prices.
Limited to the specific data it was trained on.
Requires external data access for up-to-date responses.

slides.title: Enhancing LLMs with Tools
slides.content:
LLMs can access external tools like APIs for current data.
Chat GPT's "searching the web" feature is an example.
Integrate APIs (e.g., Expedia) to fetch live information.
Enables LLMs to gather the latest flight prices.
Makes the LLM more intelligent and capable.

slides.title: LLM + Tools Analogy
slides.content:
Think of the LLM as the brain of the system.
Tools are like hammers and screwdrivers for humans.
Providing tools extends the brain's capabilities.
Allows the system to perform additional actions.
Enhances problem-solving beyond basic knowledge.

slides.title: What is an AI Agent?
slides.content:
A program designed to complete specific tasks autonomously.
Takes input, thinks, and acts to achieve a goal.
Goes beyond simple Q&A chatbots.
Utilizes tools, memory, and knowledge effectively.
Exhibits independent decision-making for narrow tasks.

slides.title: AI Agent Capabilities
slides.content:
Accesses external APIs for dynamic data and actions.
Can search, compare, and make decisions independently.
For example, finding the cheapest flight among options.
Performs actions, not just answering questions.
Often focused on a narrow and specific range of tasks.

slides.title: Simple AI Agent Example
slides.content:
Booking the cheapest flight from A to B tomorrow.
Agent uses Expedia API to search various flights.
Identifies the lowest-priced option automatically.
Proceeds to book the selected flight for the user.
Demonstrates task completion and autonomous action.

slides.title: Complex AI Agent Tasks
slides.content:
Handling multi-criteria travel planning requests.
"Travel to New Delhi in May for 7 sunny days, budget < $1600."
Integrates weather APIs to find suitable dates.
Searches flights, compares airlines, and adheres to budget.
Can suggest additional services like hotels or taxis.

slides.title: Multi-Agent Systems
slides.content:
Some complex tasks require multiple specialized AI agents.
A flight booking agent could interact with an immigration agent.
Immigration agent checks visa eligibility before booking.
Accesses immigration APIs and passport records.
Ensures visa is valid, preventing potential travel issues.

slides.title: What is Agentic AI?
slides.content:
A sophisticated system with one or more AI agents.
Works autonomously on complex, often long-duration tasks.
Makes multi-step decisions using tools and other agents.
Engages in multi-step reasoning and planning.
Aims to achieve a complex goal with high autonomy.

slides.title: Evolving AI Capabilities [COMPARISON]
slides.content:
**Generative AI:** Simple Q&A, knowledge cut-off, no tools.
**AI Agent:** Tools & memory, narrow tasks, some autonomy.
**Agentic AI:** Multiple agents, complex goals, high autonomy.
**Task Complexity:** Q&A -> Simple Task -> Multi-step Planning.
**Tool Usage:** None -> Yes (single agent) -> Yes (multiple tools/agents).
**Autonomy Level:** Lowest -> Moderate -> Highest for complex goals.

slides.title: Building Agentic AI Systems
slides.content:
Various tools and frameworks are available for development.
N8N is an example shown for visual workflow diagrams.
Generative AI (LLM) is a core component within.
Frameworks like Agnocruion aid in system creation.
Definitions can vary, but core principles remain.

slides.title: Agentic AI in Practice
slides.content:
Example: Employee onboarding system for organizations.
Agentic AI automates adding employees to HRMS.
Sends welcome emails and notifies managers automatically.
Uses a frontend (e.g., Cloud Desktop) and backend server.
Handles complex, multi-step organizational workflows.

slides.title: Key Takeaways
slides.content:
Generative AI creates content, but with knowledge limits.
AI Agents add tools for narrow task completion.
Agentic AI orchestrates agents for complex, autonomous goals.
Complexity and sophistication increase across these stages.
These concepts drive advanced AI applications and automation.
